#image("/imgs/ap-calc-bc-2009-form-b-frq-03-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

A continuous function $f$ is defined on the closed interval $- 4 <= x <= 6$. The graph of $f$ consists of a line segment and a curve that is tangent to the $x$-axis at $x = 3$, as shown in the figure above. On the interval $0 < x < 6$, the function $f$ is twice differentiable, with $f''(x)> 0$.

(a) Is $f$ differentiable at $x = 0$ ? Use the definition of the derivative with one-sided limits to justify your answer.

(b) For how many values of $a \,- 4 <= a < 6$, is the average rate of change of $f$ on the interval $\[a \, 6 \]$ equal to 0 ? Give a reason for your answer.

(c) Is there a value of $a \,- 4 <= a < 6$, for which the Mean Value Theorem, applied to the interval $\[a \, 6 \]$, guarantees a value $c \, a < c < 6$, at which $f'(c)= frac(1,3)$ ? Justify your answer.

(d) The function $g$ is defined by $g(x)= integral_(0)^(x) f(t) d t$ for $- 4 <= x <= 6$. On what intervals contained in $\[- 4 \,6 \]$ is the graph of $g$ concave up? Explain your reasoning.
